provenance: Live run on pbmc3k: Claude framed each decision, Jev answered with a calibrated probability, and two of seven answers fell below the 0.55 floor and took the step's declared default.

obs.annotation_source: jev_markers (floor 0.55, 0 abstained, 1 retried, 1 rescued by panel)

framing.stringency: This PBMC3k matrix has 2700 cells and 32738 genes measured, all from a single batch. Decide how hard to filter based on how much headroom the cell count gives you and how you expect gene-detection and mitochondrial contamination to look for a dataset of this depth and scale.
framing.flag_doublets: The dataset has 2700 cells from a single batch/lane. Decide whether this cell count is high enough that loading-rate doublets are likely to matter enough to warrant a dedicated doublet-detection pass before downstream analysis.

framing.method: This run has 2694 cells and 13714 genes from a single batch, with median counts per cell of 2197 and median genes per cell of 817 (median pct mitochondrial reads 2.03%). Depth is moderate but not extremely deep, and there is only one batch so cross-batch composition effects are not a factor here. The choice should turn on how much cell-to-cell depth variation and matrix sparsity matter for the downstream clustering/DE use of pbmc3k, given these depth and gene-count numbers.

framing.n_hvg: PBMC3k has 2694 cells and 13714 genes profiled, log1p-CPM normalized, single batch, with ground-truth labels for 2638 cells spanning the several immune cell types typically found in PBMCs (T cell subsets, B cells, monocytes, NK cells, etc.). The choice of HVG count determines how much of the ~13.7k-gene transcriptome is used to build downstream structure: fewer genes will emphasize the dominant, well-separated populations (e.g., T vs monocyte vs B), while more genes retains signal from smaller or transcriptionally similar subpopulations (e.g., NK vs CD8 T, or the small platelet/DC subsets) at the cost of more noise.
framing.n_pcs: With 2694 cells and a single batch, the PCA embedding built from the chosen HVG set will feed clustering and comparison against the 2638 ground-truth labels covering multiple PBMC cell types. The number of PCs retained controls how much fine-grained structure (e.g., closely related lymphocyte subsets) versus technical noise is carried into downstream steps on this relatively small, single-batch matrix.

framing.resolution: This PBMC dataset has 2694 cells and 2638 labelled with ground-truth identities (a PBMC reference typically resolves into roughly 8-10 major immune subsets such as T-cell subsets, B cells, NK cells, monocytes, and dendritic cells). Clustering will run on 50 PCs computed from 2000 HVGs, capturing only 13.9% of total variance, from a single batch with no integration correction needed. Judge granularity against how many biologically distinct PBMC populations this cell count and label structure can support without fragmenting a single type into spurious subclusters.

summary.source: jev_markers (floor 0.55, 0 abstained, 1 retried, 1 rescued by panel)

framing.model: This PBMC3k run produced 8 Leiden clusters at resolution 0.8 from a 2000-gene HVG space reduced to 50 PCs (only 13.9% variance explained), with a single batch and log1p-CPM normalized values. Ground-truth labels exist for 2638 of 2694 cells, suggesting a well-characterized immune cell mixture. The decision turns on whether to annotate at the cluster level using known PBMC marker genes, or to classify at the per-cell level using a pretrained reference, and how much tolerance there is for ambiguous or mixed clusters.

criteria.lenient: Shallow or precious data: keep almost everything.
criteria.standard: Healthy 10x-scale data: the usual 200-gene / 10% mito cut.
criteria.strict: Deep data with visible stress or ambient RNA: cut hard.

criteria.log1p_cpm: The default: size-factor scaling to 1e4 then log1p. Safe, well understood.
criteria.pearson_residuals: Analytic Pearson residuals: better for shallow UMI data and HVG selection.
criteria.scran_pooling: Median size factors: the rescaling target is set by the data rather than a fixed constant. Best with strong composition differences between cells.

decisions.question: model
decisions.instructions: This PBMC3k run produced 8 Leiden clusters at resolution 0.8 from a 2000-gene HVG space reduced to 50 PCs (only 13.9% variance explained), with a single batch and log1p-CPM normalized values. Ground-truth labels exist for 2638 of 2694 cells, suggesting a well-characterized immune cell mixture. The decision turns on whether to annotate at the cluster level using known PBMC marker genes, or to classify at the per-cell level using a pretrained reference, and how much tolerance there is for ambiguous or mixed clusters.

criteria.markers_llm: Claude reads the top marker genes per cluster and names it. No reference model and no GPU; strongest when the tissue is well described in the literature and the clusters are clean.
criteria.celltypist: Logistic-regression classifier over curated references. Per-cell rather than per-cluster, CPU-cheap; strongest when a reference model matching this tissue exists.
criteria.jev_markers: Jev scores each cluster's marker genes against a fixed cell-type vocabulary and returns a calibrated probability per type. Per-cluster, sub-second, and the only option that can decline to answer when the markers are ambiguous.
